text: A few weeks after both pages go live, Finance emails: our weekly refund total jumped, and it doesn't line up with what Support shows for refunded tickets. It jumped isn't enough to act on yet. The first job is reproducing it reliably, on your own screen, before touching a single Task.

Opening vw_finance_refunds for that week and looking closely at individual subscribers turns up this: two rows with the exact same ticket ID and the exact same updated_at timestamp, both contributing to the same week's total. That's not a second refund — a genuine new refund would carry its own, different timestamp. It's the same event, counted twice.

Checking refund_event_count against the number of distinct refunded ticket IDs, across several weeks, shows a pattern: most weeks, the two numbers match exactly. In a handful of specific weeks, refund_event_count runs consistently a few rows higher — never dramatic, never in Support's numbers, only in Finance's.

A random one-off glitch might suggest a data-quality problem in the source JSON. A small, structurally consistent gap, specific to refund_events, points somewhere much more specific: something is writing to that table more than once for the same underlying change. Recall from Lesson 6, finance_refund_task's MERGE is append-only and explicitly not idempotent — unlike ticket_facts_sync_task's. That's a strong lead, not an accusation yet.
Don't delete anything, don't rewrite the MERGE, don't suspend any Task yet. Next lesson confirms the actual cause using Snowflake's own task history, before anything changes.
